samples.text: I myself, in 2015, as Minister for Internal Affairs and Communications, attended the United Nations World Conference on Disaster Reduction, where the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction was adopted. Promoting this framework remains one of our top priorities to this day. It is in Sendai that Japan will host the Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in October next year. To protect the lives of present and future generations, all states must take serious action to tackle global warming. I believe that climate action and economic growth can go hand in hand. Japan has been advancing green transformation GX efforts with the goal of achieving net zero by 2050. Such capabilities include establishing the basis for the production and engineering of materials such as green steel, utilizing the world's most efficient gas fire power generation, and popularizing the adoption of energy efficient data centers. harnessing Japan's technological capabilities. We will enhance these efforts with a view to strengthening the resilience of the energy supply demand structure and vigorously advance the policy package for wide energy and resources resilience through green transformation or power GX. Furthermore, Japan will contribute to global climate action, including through GX related efforts such as the Asia Zero Emission Community. that simultaneously achieve decarbonization, energy security, and economic growth. Next year, Japan will host the World Horticultural Exposition 2027 in Yokohama, which is an industrial trade fair showcasing green technologies and approaches to sustainable development. We sincerely hope that many of you will come to join this expo. There are also challenges arising from technological innovation. While advances in AI bring tremendous opportunities for humanity, they also pose challenges, including those related to national security. We also urgently need measures to tackle the spread of information not based on facts, as well as the spread of propaganda. Japan took the initiative to launch the Hiroshima AI Process, establishing the world's first international world's first international principles and code of conduct to govern generative AI.

The second issue is how to strike a balance between the progress of digitalization and human dignity. Digitalization is bringing benefits to all; however, there are risks of privacy and human rights violations. We need a digital ecosystem and international rules that are compatible with human dignity. That is why, at the G-7 Hiroshima Summit, we launched the Hiroshima Artificial Intelligence (AI) Process on generative AI, towards attaining trustworthy AI. Japan will also strengthen its support for digitalization in developing countries while ensuring cybersecurity.

“Among such digital technologies, there is an urgent need to establish international governance on artificial intelligence (AI) in order to maximize the opportunities brought by AI while mitigating its risks. Japan has been working through the Hiroshima AI Process to achieve safe, secure and trustworthy AI. We will continue to actively contribute to the discussions on AI at the United Nations.

In parallel, Japan has been working with like-minded partners and Global South partners to co-create a safe, secure, and trustworthy AI ecosystem and will enhance cooperation on safety to respond to the risks of highly capable frontier AI. To accelerate these efforts, we intend to host an AI summit in Japan at the earliest opportunity. Madam President, since the end of the Second World War, Japan has built the peace and prosperity it has today through the tireless efforts of our predecessors and the goodwill of a large number of countries. In the course of these efforts, Japan itself has consistently acted in the spirit of multilateralism towards addressing challenges facing the international community. However, these challenges cannot be solved by any single country acting alone. Now more than ever, the flag of the United Nations must be held high, and under that banner, member states must mobilize the collective strength of the membership to elaborate new rules and build a framework for cooperation. I am convinced that the United Nations is the only organization capable of taking the helm on a global scale. To this end as well, reform of the United Nations is essential. The United Nations is a vessel and the responsibility for determining its contents lies with us, namely the member states. Rather than lamenting the institutional fatigue of the United Nations, member states should unite with one heart, vigorously advance reform of the United Nations, and transform the organization into a more resilient and effective United Nations. Let us move forward, building on the achievements of the current Secretary-General, Antonio Guterres. At the same time, the Charter of the United Nations, which is now 81 years old, should also be reviewed. Regarding the so-called enemy states clauses, a United Nations General Assembly resolution was adopted in 2005 to delete references to enemy states from the Charter of the United Nations, expressing the resolve of the heads of state and government of all member states. In accordance with this resolution, these clauses must be deleted.
